nodes.title: How to use this workflow
widgets_values:
# Contact matching: one entity id per contact

1. On **Input · exports**, press **Upload data files** and pick your contacts, phones and addresses CSV files (or choose a folder in ComfyUI's input folder). On **1 · Read the exports**, say in the **Column map** which column holds what.
2. Press **Run**. With no reviews yet, pairs are scored by their agreement patterns; the **Review** tab asks you about the pairs the model is least sure of. Decide them, run again: each round it learns from all your reviews. About 1,000 reviews is enough.
3. **Match at** on **6 · Decide** sets how sure a merge must be. The results: **entities** (every contact with its entity id) and **review_queue** (the pairs for people to decide).
4. To try it on generated data: run **Studio - Contact matching benchmark** first (it writes contacts_benchmark/company_hard_10000_7).
5. **Export as Python** (Contract tab) turns it into a command-line program for your own machines.

widgets_values_named.text:
# Contact matching: one entity id per contact

1. On **Input · exports**, press **Upload data files** and pick your contacts, phones and addresses CSV files (or choose a folder in ComfyUI's input folder). On **1 · Read the exports**, say in the **Column map** which column holds what.
2. Press **Run**. With no reviews yet, pairs are scored by their agreement patterns; the **Review** tab asks you about the pairs the model is least sure of. Decide them, run again: each round it learns from all your reviews. About 1,000 reviews is enough.
3. **Match at** on **6 · Decide** sets how sure a merge must be. The results: **entities** (every contact with its entity id) and **review_queue** (the pairs for people to decide).
4. To try it on generated data: run **Studio - Contact matching benchmark** first (it writes contacts_benchmark/company_hard_10000_7).
5. **Export as Python** (Contract tab) turns it into a command-line program for your own machines.

decisions.decision: A model learns the weights from your reviews (logistic regression, active learning).
decisions.why: it beat fixed rules, Fellegi–Sunter and gradient boosting in every trial
neither improved the result at 100,000 contacts (research/contacts_er/RESULTS.md)
decisions.instead_of: a dense index and a cross-encoder

decisions.decision: Uncertain pairs and disputed reviews go to you.
decisions.why: a wrong merge costs more than a question

decisions.decision: Its quality comes from your reviews: about 1,000 make it good. Review a round, run again; a larger round (reviews per round 200) means fewer runs.
decisions.why: measured on the company_hard 10k synthetic benchmark: no reviews F1 0.54 (precision 0.85, recall 0.39); 1,000 reviews F1 0.96 (precision 0.98, recall 0.93)
decisions.instead_of: fixed weights tuned on synthetic data, which would not fit yours
decisions.principle: learn from the data it runs on
